cues: Must is felt from inside, or comes from the speaker: I must stop wasting time.
Have to comes from outside, from rules or other people: we have to wear the college uniform.
Had to is the past of both, because must has no past: yesterday I had to work late, never I must worked.
And should, or ought to, is a weaker duty: a citizen ought to pay tax.
